summary: Template literals build text from values. toFixed(), padStart(), and padEnd() control decimal places, column width, and alignment for reports, receipts, and tables.
notes: average.toFixed(2) returns the string "87.46". It does not change the value stored in average.
courses[i].padEnd(12) pads the text to 12 characters. padStart() works only on strings, so call toFixed() on a number first.
In `$${raised}` the first $ is a plain dollar sign. ${ starts the value.
pitfall: Using quotes instead of backticks prints the braces literally: "${student}" shows ${student} instead of Jordan.
contrast: Template literals (`${average}`) work like Python's f-strings, but JavaScript has no format codes like :.2f or %.2f. You call methods instead: toFixed(2) for decimals and padStart() or padEnd() for width.
